Getting started

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

This document is for anyone writing a new Shiny app who wants to add authentication in half an hour. How the package works and what it protects against is described in the architecture-and-security vignette; how to migrate an app that is already running is covered in integrating-existing-app.

What you need

  • The package installed: library(appauth).
  • A database for the app: a SQLite file (the default) or DuckDB, MySQL / MariaDB or PostgreSQL (see the deployment vignette, section “Other databases”). The package creates its own tables in it (users, auth_sessions, login_attempts, appauth_migrations and others) and does not touch the app’s other tables.
  • A decision on how the app determines permissions: a “permission -> roles” matrix or something of your own. More on this below and in the extension-points vignette.

Basic concepts

  • User: login, role, blocked flag. The password is stored only as a scrypt hash.
  • Role: one of settings$roles (by default admin, user, viewer). The settings$admin_role role manages users; you define the other permissions.
  • Permission: the name of an action or section, for example "Run" or "Access". A role has a set of permissions, determined by the permission provider (provider).
  • Session: the signed-in user (auth$user()) and, if auto-login is on, their token in a cookie.
  • Event: the package writes nothing to logs itself; it reports events (login_failed, user_blocked…) to the on_event function that you define.

Five steps

1. Settings 

library(shiny)
library(appauth)

settings <- aa_settings()   # the defaults suit most apps

Settings can be read from config.yaml: aa_settings_from_list(conf$security). All parameters are listed in ?aa_settings.

2. Permissions 

provider <- aa_permissions_from_matrix(list(
  Tasks  = c("admin", "user", "viewer"),
  Run    = c("admin", "user"),
  Access = "admin"
))

The administrator role does not get permissions by itself: only those listed in the matrix.

3. User interface 

ui <- fluidPage(
  aa_app_head(),          # styles and the cookie script, once per page
  aa_auth_ui("auth"),     # login form
  uiOutput("main")        # the rest of the app
)

4. Server 

log_event <- function(event, user, session_id, value) {
  message(sprintf("[appauth] %s user=%s value=%s", event, user, value))
}

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # the connection closes together with the session; the schema is prepared on connect
  conn <- aa_session_connection("app.db", prepare = TRUE, settings = settings)

  # login, first administrator creation, auto-login, logout
  auth <- aa_auth_server("auth", conn, settings, on_event = log_event)

  # blocking, deletion, role change and password reset take effect within 30 seconds
  aa_session_guard(auth, conn, settings)

  # the server part of a tab is attached only for those who have the permission
  aa_register_module(auth, "Access", provider, function() {
    aa_users_server("users", conn, auth, settings, on_event = log_event)
  })

  output$main <- renderUI({
    req(auth$logged_in())
    user <- auth$user()

    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("Tasks",
        p("Signed in as ", strong(user$login)),
        if (aa_can(user, "Run", provider)) actionButton("run", "Run")
      ),
      if (aa_can(user, "Access", provider)) tabPanel("Access", aa_users_ui("users")),
      tabPanel("Sign out", actionButton("logout", "Sign out"))
    )
  })

  observeEvent(input$run, {
    # the permission is checked on the server: a hidden button is not protection
    aa_require(auth, "Run", provider, on_event = log_event, settings = settings)
    showNotification("Done")
  })

  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout(reload = TRUE))
}

5. Run 

shinyApp(ui, server)

On an empty database the app offers to create the first administrator. After that the administrator adds users on the “Access” tab. Ready-to-run versions are in system.file("examples", package = "appauth").

How it works without Shiny

All features are also available as plain functions. This is handy for scripts, tests and administrative tasks:

library(appauth)

conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")
aa_init_db(conn)                                   # creates the tables

aa_create_first_admin(conn, "boss", "boss-password")
#> [1] TRUE
aa_create_user(conn, "ivan", "ivan-password", "user")

aa_list_users(conn)                                # password hashes are not returned
#>   login  role blocked          created_at last_login_at
#> 1  boss admin       0 2026-11-20 06:34:35          <NA>
#> 2  ivan  user       0 2026-11-20 06:34:35          <NA>

aa_authenticate(conn, "ivan", "ivan-password")     # user data
#>   login role blocked must_change
#> 1  ivan user       0           0
is.null(aa_authenticate(conn, "ivan", "wrong"))    # wrong password: NULL
#> [1] TRUE

Auto-login token and permission check:

token <- aa_issue_token(conn, "ivan")              # token for the cookie
aa_find_session_user(conn, token)                  # the user is found by the token
#> $login
#> [1] "ivan"
#> 
#> $role
#> [1] "user"

provider <- aa_permissions_from_matrix(list(Tasks = c("admin", "user"), Access = "admin"))
aa_can(list(login = "ivan", role = "user"), "Tasks", provider)
#> [1] TRUE
aa_can(list(login = "ivan", role = "user"), "Access", provider)
#> [1] FALSE

Blocking a user revokes their tokens:

aa_set_blocked(conn, "ivan", TRUE, acting_login = "boss")
is.null(aa_find_session_user(conn, token))
#> [1] TRUE

User rules are enforced automatically and report a clear reason:

tryCatch(
  aa_delete_user(conn, "boss", acting_login = "boss"),
  appauth_error_user = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
#> [1] "You cannot delete yourself"

DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)

What to customize

Need How
Other roles aa_settings(roles = c("owner", "editor"), admin_role = "owner")
Stricter brute-force protection aa_settings(max_failed_logins = 3, lockout_minutes = 30)
Password length aa_settings(password_min = 10)
Weak passwords: reject or do not check aa_settings(password_policy = "reject") or "off" (default "warn": accept and warn)
No auto-login aa_settings(autologin = FALSE)
Russian interface aa_settings(texts = aa_texts("ru"))
Custom button text aa_texts("en", login_button = "Log in to the system")
Permanent administrator password aa_settings(must_change_default = FALSE)
Two-factor authentication (TOTP) aa_settings(totp_enabled = TRUE, totp_key = ...) and aa_totp_server() in the user’s account page, recipe in the extension-points vignette
Password reset by email aa_settings(reset_enabled = TRUE, send_reset = ..., reset_base_url = ...), recipe in the extension-points vignette
Your own permissions (not a matrix) a function(user) instead of aa_permissions_from_matrix()
Your own block in the user card extra_card_ui and extra_card_server in aa_users_server()
Where to write events the on_event function in all modules; ready-made handler: aa_event_logger()
Changing your own password and “sign out on all devices” aa_password_server() and auth$logout_all(), recipe in the extension-points vignette

Details and examples are in the extension-points vignette.

FAQ

Why aa_register_module() if there is aa_require()? They are different things. Registration saves unnecessary work for those without the permission, while aa_require() protects against forged requests: the permission is checked again in every action handler.

What does aa_session_guard() do? At a regular interval it checks the open session. If the user was blocked, deleted, had their role changed or their password reset, the session ends. Without it such changes take effect only at the next login.

Can I pass aa_auth_server() a connection that I open myself? Yes, but then you must close it yourself in session$onSessionEnded(). Otherwise the database file stays busy until the process stops, and on Windows such a file cannot be renamed. aa_session_connection() does this for you.

What happened to plaintext passwords? The package does not accept them: a plaintext password in the database will not let anyone sign in. How to safely migrate such passwords to hashes is described in the integrating-existing-app vignette.
